about: Movie themes for the agent-teams console. A theme renames agents, gives each character a hand-drawn 32x32 portrait, and — with film palette on — sets the console's ground and accent.
It never renames a state, a verb, a metric, a task id or a file path — those are readouts.
There is no UI for this file; it is the data the console reads.
There is also no separate 'movie theme' picker: films are entries in the one 'theme' dropdown in the config panel (gear), under a FILM group after SYSTEM.

rules.castingIsByRoleSlot: Map characters to role slots, never hashed from agent ids. The same role in the same film must always be the same character, so a theme is learnable.
rules.portraitsAreFiles: Each character in themes[].roles has a hand-drawn 32x32 portrait at src/web/images/characters-v3/<film>/<Name>.svg, compiled into src/shared/portraits-v3.ts by npm run build:portraits and keyed by this theme's key and the role's exact name. It is drawn only at integer multiples of 32px and never recoloured. A spare, an agent past the slots, and the off theme keep the role sprite.
rules.typeBadgeStays: The agent-type badge stays beside the character name. 'Ariadne' + an 'architect' badge costs no information; replacing the type makes the wall unreadable.
rules.mentionMatchesEither: @ filters on the character name AND the real slot name, and shows the slot name beside the character.
rules.overflowKeepsRealNames: A team with more agents than the theme has role slots leaves the extras under their real names. Draw from 'spare' only if you need more named agents; never invent characters.
rules.oneMapping: Feed every view from a single asChar(slot) mapping — wall, overview, rail, grid, panel chips, task owners, mailbox runs, comms thread pairs and bubbles, mention picker.
rules.teamNameIsDecoration: The in-world team name is a chip on the session-picker trigger only. The real session id is untouched everywhere else. Measure the status bar in the LONGEST team-name state, not the default.
rules.firstLightIsData: The empty-team state's kicker, headline and body live here per theme as firstLight, with {lead} as a literal placeholder the console fills with the lead's character name ('lead' with no theme). Copy is data, so a new film needs no code.
rules.paletteIsTheGrade: A film palette is read from the light the story is shot in, never from artwork, a logo or a title card. Ground, text and one accent ramp; the neutral ramp is inherited from the base theme named in palette.neutralsFrom so contrast is never left to chance.
rules.paletteIsASwitch: The film palette is a toggle, defaulting on. Off, a theme sets names and portrait colours only — that is the escape hatch for anyone who wants their own scheme, and the reason the old names-only rule can be retired without argument.
rules.noSemanticRecolour: warn and fail are declared per palette, never derived, because a semantic colour has to survive next to THIS accent. A film whose accent is red cannot also draw failure in red (Reservoir Dogs, Pulp Fiction shift fail to a rose); a film whose accent is gold cannot draw attention in amber (Inception, LOTR, The Godfather shift warn to a lighter rose-orange, a different hue from their accent and a different lightness from their fail). Check both pairs, not just fail.
rules.onePicker: Films live in the same dropdown as the system colour themes, not in a picker of their own — two lists that both change the console's appearance is one list. A 'film palette' toggle appears only while a film is selected: off, the film renames agents and tints portraits while the ground stays on the system theme.
rules.accentsFollowTheTheme: A system theme offers its four accent schemes. A film carries ONE accent ramp — its own — so the four-swatch row is replaced by that single swatch. Never invent four variants of somebody else’s grade.
rules.oneAccentRamp: A film carries one accent ramp, so the four-swatch accent row is replaced by that film's own — never four invented variants of somebody's grade.

legal: Character names are protected IP, and so is a film’s visual identity. Palettes here are hand-picked colours in the spirit of each film’s grade, and the portraits are stylised hand-drawn 32x32 pixel characters — not artwork from the films, not likenesses. Fine for a personal or internal tool; not for anything shipped publicly.

firstLight.kicker: A TEAM OF ONE, FOR NOW
firstLight.head: {lead} is here. Nobody else yet.
firstLight.body: Teammates show up here when the lead spawns them. Until then it’s a quiet room, and a quiet room is fine.

themes.note: the dream heist — its cast is already named by function

firstLight.kicker: THE CREW IS STILL ON THE PLANE
firstLight.head: {lead} is awake. Everyone else is a level down.
firstLight.body: Arthur, Eames and the rest arrive when {lead} needs them. If they never do, check your totem and carry on.

palette.label: steel & kick
palette.why: the film grades cold steel against the warm of the kick; the accent is that warmth

firstLight.kicker: THE PARTY IS STILL ON THEIR BIKES
firstLight.head: {lead} is here. The rest are still at the arcade.
firstLight.body: Nobody has radioed in yet. The party shows up when {lead} calls them, usually right before something goes wrong.

palette.label: Hawkins red
palette.why: dark teal small town, the Upside Down bleeding red through it

firstLight.head: {lead} is here. The others are still at second breakfast.
firstLight.body: One does not simply spawn a fellowship. They arrive when {lead} asks, and not a moment before.

palette.label: gold & pine
palette.why: deep pine and earth, with the one gold thing everybody wants

firstLight.kicker: THE REBELLION IS STILL IN HYPERSPACE
firstLight.head: {lead} is here. Everyone else is still in hyperspace.
firstLight.body: The rest of the rebellion drops out of lightspeed when {lead} sends the signal. Chewbacca has been told to stop roaring at the log.

palette.label: saber blue
palette.why: black space, and the only light source that matters is a blade

firstLight.kicker: THE GARAGE IS STILL AT 87 MPH
firstLight.head: {lead} got here first. Everyone else is still accelerating.
firstLight.body: The rest of the garage arrives when {lead} needs them. Roads, at this stage, are optional.

palette.label: flux cyan
palette.why: night-blue Hill Valley lit by electrical discharge

firstLight.head: {lead} is here. Everyone else is still deciding what to order.
firstLight.body: The outfit gets called in when there’s a problem worth solving. The Wolf only comes if it’s a real one.

palette.label: diner red
palette.why: vinyl-booth red on warm black — the film lives indoors at night

firstLight.kicker: THE FAMILY HAS NOT BEEN SENT FOR
firstLight.head: {lead} is here. The family hasn’t been sent for.
firstLight.body: {lead} will make them an offer when there’s work. Until then, nobody gets a visit.

palette.label: sodium dark
palette.why: business conducted after dark, lit by a desk lamp

themes.note: the cast is a colour list — names and accents are the same set

firstLight.kicker: THE JOB IS FIVE PEOPLE SHORT
firstLight.head: {lead} is here. The job is five people short.
firstLight.body: Everyone else turns up when {lead} hands out the colours. Nobody gets to be Mr. Black.

palette.label: black, white, red
palette.why: black suits, white shirts, one colour that is not either

firstLight.kicker: THE NEB HAS NOT JACKED IN
firstLight.head: {lead} is in. Nobody else has taken the pill.
firstLight.body: The rest of the crew jacks in when {lead} calls the operator. Until then there is no team. There is only the lead.

palette.label: phosphor
palette.why: you are inside the screen, so the screen colour is the world colour

themes.note: the show colour-codes its cast on purpose

firstLight.kicker: THE LAB IS STILL AN RV
firstLight.head: {lead} is here. The lab is still an RV.
firstLight.body: The rest of the crew gets called in when {lead} says the word. Until then it’s one chemist in a parking lot.

palette.label: desert lab
palette.why: the show colour-codes on purpose; this is its desert yellow-green
